A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Double Binary Factorization work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and references support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v3 reports original DBF compression accuracy, nonuniform compression results, reconstruction-error analyses, and GPU speed measurements in Section 4.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds MMLU/GSM8k evaluations, size-annealing results, and reconstruction experiments on larger-model matrices.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a size-annealing variant that starts with a smaller middle dimension and gradually expands it, changing the factorization procedure for that experiment. The main DBF representation, alternating optimization, importance scaling, PV-tuning, and nonuniform compression algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds MMLU academic-knowledge and GSM8k arithmetic-reasoning evaluation for Llama3-8B at 2–2.3 bits, substantially broadening the tested capabilities beyond v3's perplexity and commonsense/science-question benchmarks. The existing calibration data and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Caldera is added to the Llama2-7B and Llama3-8B comparisons in Tables 1 and 2, with entries at 2.1 and 2.4 bits. The previous comparator membership within each table is otherwise unchanged.

E3.justification: The added evaluations use 5-shot MMLU and 8-shot GSM8k protocols. Figure 3 also extends reconstruction testing to selected Llama3-70B and Llama3.1-405B matrices. Existing calibration counts, fine-tuning budgets, and batch-size-one speed protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 3 add experiments testing whether size annealing alleviates higher-bit reconstruction error and whether reconstruction quality deteriorates for much larger matrices. These substantially expand the diagnostic analysis beyond v3's weight-importance study and bitwidth comparison on two Llama3-8B layers.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds Caldera results, the MMLU/GSM8k results in Table 3, and annealing/scaling findings in Figure 3. At 2.3 bits, DBF + PV versus AQLM + PV scores 56.37 versus 56.20 on MMLU and 27.59 versus 35.25 on GSM8k. The retained uniform-compression, nonuniform-compression, and speed results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The factorization equations, optimization objectives, ADMM updates, and channel-importance formula are retained. The new diagonal-Fisher analogy is an intuitive interpretation, without a formal definition, derivation, or proof; notation corrections do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the claims of competitive low-bit compression, flexible compression ratios, nonuniform allocation, and practical speedups. The title and compression-flexibility wording are refined without materially redefining those contributions.

C2.justification: v3 leaves the cause of higher-bit weakness unresolved; v4 interprets annealing improvements as suggesting an algorithmic rather than fundamental limitation. It also adds the diagonal-Fisher intuition, qualifies reasoning results as coming from untuned pretrained models, and reports the 405B higher-bit memory limitation.

D1.justification: v4 documents the annealing schedule: 80% of iterations at a 2-bit middle dimension, followed by gradual expansion during the final 20%, with small random initialization. Figure 3 identifies the 40GB GPU memory constraint. Existing implementation, compute-budget, and code-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of Caldera, SVD-LLM, SVD-LLM v2, and Cherniuk et al.'s quantization-aware factorization, including distinctions from DBF. References for MMLU and GSM8k are also added. This is a focused expansion of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from compressing neural networks to compressing large language models, with localized grammar corrections, abbreviation clarification, and explanatory additions. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adopts TMLR typography, headers, author formatting, and page geometry. Figure 3 expands from two panels to four with an additional curve and revised legend/caption; Table 3 is added and Tables 1–2 gain Caldera rows. The unchanged speed tables are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical completeness through the Caldera comparison, reasoning benchmarks that reveal a GSM8k weakness, and experiments addressing v3's unresolved higher-bit behavior. These additions support a more informative assessment of DBF. The gains remain limited: larger-model evidence concerns individual matrices, and annealing provides suggestive evidence rather than establishing the cause of the higher-bit limitation.
